Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

army noun

also armies, troops, forces, join the army, raise an army, review the army, review the troops, a large force, a small force, concentrate the troops, crack troops, call up the troops, supply with men and arms

classical

Phaedr. 4.6.1
Liv. 21.33.11
Traupman 185

exercitus, exercitūs m.

noun, fourth declension

From exercēre: a trained body of men (Lewis & Short). To raise an army, exercitum comparāre (Traupman 185); to join the army, in mīlitiam īre (Traupman 183).

Other words

  • cōpiae, cōpiārum f. pl. — troops, forces

    noun, first declension, plural · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.48 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 186

    The forces, as made up of their units; rarely in the singular (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • cum victī mūrēs mustēlārum exercitū … fugerent

    when the mice, beaten by the weasels’ army, were running awayPhaedr. 4.6.1–3

  • captō cibō ac pecoribus per trīduum exercitum aluit

    with the food and cattle he had captured he fed the army for three daysLiv. 21.33.11

  • exercitum comparāre

    to raise an armyTraupman 185

  • exercitum recēnsēre (lūstrāre)

    to review the armyTraupman 187; cf. Liv. 1.16: exercitum recēnsēre; Cic. Att. 5.20.2: exercitum lūstrāvī (Lewis & Short)

  • magnae (exiguae) cōpiae

    a large (small) forceTraupman 186

  • omnēs cōpiās in ūnum locum cōgere

    to concentrate all the troops in one placeTraupman 186

  • ēvocāre cōpiās

    to call up the troopsTraupman 186

  • rōbora peditum

    crack infantry troopsTraupman 186

  • alicui virōs et arma ministrāre

    to supply someone with men and armsTraupman 188

See also soldier, war, battle, enemy.
